Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-prompt-long-0085", "row_sha256": "1ddd07644ef939b478958e4115f4d2292ca7ed84d769315181dc87b3fc0fa1ee", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "can you help me put together a local newspaper correction update for the north county ledger, about something in the may 14 web story and the may 16 print edition? i need one self-contained, ordinary update that readers can understand without looking up a long chain of coverage. this is a new fictional episode based on these details, not a request for a full new article about the whole water program. please organize what i’m giving you into a usable prompt for that update; don’t write the update itself.

the story was about the county environmental office’s free water-sampling event at the old mill street depot in bellwether. the notice said residents could drop off household water samples and pick up sample kits. the event is scheduled for sunday, june 28, 2026, from 9 a.m. until 1 p.m. the problem is that the paper’s notice gave june 18 as the date. it was printed that way in the may 16 edition and also appeared in the may 14 web story. those are the two places i’m asking the correction to address. don’t make it sound as if the paper got the location, the hours, or the services wrong too; those details are correct according to the information we have.

i’d like the update to state plainly that june 18 was incorrect and that the correct date is june 28. the correction should explain the practical reason someone reading the notice needs to know: the event is on june 28, not june 18. include the full event date and the hours, and identify the old mill street depot in bellwether so nobody has to guess which event is being corrected. say that the county environmental office is organizing it and that the event remains free. the office says residents can drop off household water samples and pick up sample kits there. don’t turn that into a claim that people can have their water tested on site, since i haven’t given you that information. also don’t suggest the event was canceled or moved; the error was in the printed date, not a change to the event.

there’s a quote from county environmental office spokesperson lena ortiz that can be used as an ordinary reported quote: “The date in the notice was wrong. We’ll be at the depot on June 28, and residents can still bring household samples or pick up a kit.” please keep the words in the quotation as supplied if you include it. identify ortiz as a spokesperson for the county environmental office. don’t invent another quote, a response from the newspaper, or an explanation for how the wrong date got into the story. i don’t know the cause, so the update should not speculate about a typo, an editing mistake, a calendar mix-up, or who entered the date.

it would be useful to include a short numbered section if it fits naturally, but don’t force numbering if it makes a simple correction awkward. if used, the numbered part should be a compact set of the confirmed event details, not a list of proposed follow-up actions. the update should be readable as a newspaper item rather than a memo to staff. keep it calm and direct, with the correction near the start. don’t write an apology on behalf of the paper because i haven’t supplied one, and don’t add contact information, links, registration instructions, parking directions, eligibility rules, or details about what happens to samples. none of those are in the facts i have.

please distinguish the original notice from the corrected information so no reader could mistake june 18 for the event date. mention both publication locations and dates: the may 14 web story and the may 16 print edition. don’t imply that there were additional editions or that the correction has already been posted somewhere else. this should be one update covering the same date error in those two places. you can say the correct event details are confirmed by the county environmental office, but don’t present that as a separate independent investigation or suggest the office approved the wording of the newspaper correction.

one detail that matters for scope: the correct hours are still 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., and the depot remains the location. the correction is about the date only. the office describes the event as free, and that remains part of the information readers need. don’t broaden the item into general advice about drinking water, lead, sampling procedures, or other county services. there are no facts here about test results, contamination, how many residents are expected, or how many kits are available, so leave those subjects out instead of filling in plausible details. don’t add a general health warning or imply that anyone’s water is unsafe.

the final part of the update should retain my current assessment and its limits, rather than replacing it with a sweeping summary: based on what we have now, the error appears limited to the date in this event notice; the location, hours, free status, and described services match the county environmental office’s information. that assessment covers only this notice in the may 14 web story and may 16 print edition. we have not reviewed the rest of either publication for other errors, so don’t say there were no other errors or that the rest of the story was verified. if a sentence needs to reflect the review limit, make clear that the conclusion is only about the specific event details listed here, not about every detail in either publication. end with that scoped assessment as a distinct final paragraph, without adding a concluding recommendation or inventing what the paper will do next.", "output": "Write one self-contained, clear local newspaper correction update for the North County Ledger. The update should cover the same date error in the May 14 web story and the May 16 print edition. It should read like a brief newspaper item, not a staff memo, and should not become a new article about the wider water program. Put the correction near the beginning and distinguish the incorrect date from the correct event details.

The notice concerned the county environmental office’s free water-sampling event at the old Mill Street depot in Bellwether. The May 14 web story and May 16 print edition gave the event date as June 18, 2026. That date was incorrect. The correct date is Sunday, June 28, 2026, from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. State plainly that the event is on June 28, not June 18. The location, hours, free status, and described services are correct: residents can drop off household water samples and pick up sample kits at the depot. Do not suggest that water testing is available on site, that the event was canceled or moved, or that any detail besides the date was wrong.

You may include this ordinary reported quote from Lena Ortiz, a spokesperson for the county environmental office, keeping its wording unchanged if used: “The date in the notice was wrong. We’ll be at the depot on June 28, and residents can still bring household samples or pick up a kit.” Do not invent another quote, a newspaper response, or an explanation for how the incorrect date appeared. The cause is unknown; do not speculate that it was a typo, editing mistake, calendar mix-up, or the work of a particular person. You may say the correct event details are confirmed by the county environmental office, but do not describe this as an independent investigation or suggest the office approved the newspaper’s wording.

Mention both publication locations and dates: the May 14 web story and the May 16 print edition. Do not imply that there were other editions or that the correction has already been posted elsewhere. Keep the update calm and direct. A compact numbered section listing confirmed event details may be used if it fits naturally, but do not force numbering. If included, it should not list follow-up actions.

Do not write an apology on behalf of the paper or add contact information, links, registration instructions, parking directions, eligibility rules, or details about what happens to samples. Do not broaden the item into general advice about drinking water, lead, sampling procedures, or other county services. No information has been supplied about test results, contamination, expected attendance, or the number of kits, so leave those subjects out. Do not add a health warning or imply anyone’s water is unsafe.

End with a distinct final paragraph that retains this limited assessment: based on the information currently available, the error appears limited to the date in this event notice; the location, hours, free status, and described services match the county environmental office’s information. This assessment applies only to the notice in the May 14 web story and May 16 print edition. The rest of either publication has not been reviewed for other errors, so do not say there were no other errors or that the rest of the story was verified. Make clear that the assessment concerns only the specific event details given here. Do not add a concluding recommendation or state what the newspaper will do next."}]
